Government of Colombia accepts d2w Biodegradability Evidence

Symphony Environmental Technologies plc (AIM: SYM) ("Symphony" or the "Company"), the global specialist in technologies that make plastic products smarter, safer and more sustainable, announces an important development in Colombia. The Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development has accepted evidence of biodegradability and non-toxicity submitted for products made with Symphony’s d2w biodegradable masterbatch.

The submission was made under Article 34 of Law 2232 of 2022 and Article 19 of Resolution 0803 of 2024 (Annex VIII), which allows biodegradable alternatives to prohibited single-use plastic products if they satisfy the required criteria for biodegradation, and substances of concern.

The submission was made by PROMOCIONES FANTASTICAS S.A.S. ("PF"), for their polypropylene drinking-straws, and the Ministry has confirmed that the evidence satisfies the required criteria.  PF have an exclusive supply of d2w masterbatch for the manufacture of d2w drinking straws within their agreed territory.
Although the Ministry does not issue product approvals, it has confirmed that the evidence submitted for PF’s drinking straws made with d2w technology supports the statutory requirements.
Michael Laurier, Chief Executive Officer of Symphony Environmental, said:

"This is an important breakthrough after a lengthy and detailed process to satisfy the Colombian authorities.  It strengthens PF’s commercial position in Colombia, which has a population of 54 million, and is likely to increase sales of Symphony’s d2w masterbatch. It raises the acceptability and visibility of d2w across Latin America, and supports wider engagement by Symphony with manufacturers and retailers seeking practical, low-cost, alternatives to a range of prohibited single-use plastics.

Although this acknowledgement relates specifically to PF's straws, it sends a strong signal to the market: it confirms that a plastic product using d2w masterbatch comfortably meets the threshold criteria set out in the Single-Use Plastics Law to qualify as a biodegradable plastic alternative and, on that basis, to be exempt from prohibition. This should give potential users worldwide the reassurance they need to adopt the technology and continue bringing their products to market.

This development is an important addition to our recent announcement of further scientific confirmation, after extensive research, by Intertek, and by the public laboratory (CIQA) in Mexico, that plastic products made with a d2w masterbatch will biodegrade if they get into the open environment and will not leave microplastics or toxicity.”

In addition to its d2w biodegradable plastic technology - www.d2w.net - Symphony supplies a range of plastic technologies under its d2p (designed to protect) brand - www.d2p.net - to provide protection against insects, viruses, bacteria, fungi, rodents, odours, food deterioration and fire.
Symphony also provides marker technology under its d2t brand to enable proof of recycled content of plastic products and to prevent counterfeiting Taggant Technology | Symphony Environmental
Symphony has also introduced a new product under its NbR brand – www.nbr.technology  to reduce the amount of fossil-derived material in plastic products.

Symphony has a diverse and growing customer-base and has established itself over more than 30 years as an international business with over 70 distributors around the world. Products made with Symphony's plastic technologies are now available in nearly 100 countries and in many different product applications. Symphony itself is certified according to ISO9001 and ISO14001, and has held the London Stock Exchange’s Green Economy Mark since its launch in 2019.

Symphony participates in the Committee work of the British Standards Institute (BSI), the American Standards Organisation (ASTM), the European Standards Organisation (CEN), and the International Standards Organisation (ISO).
Further information on the Group can be found at www.symphonyenvironmental.com
